proof_summary: After establishing integrality by prime-adic valuation estimates (using multiplicative orders, LTE, and Legendre’s formula), the recurrence \((m+1)a(m+1)=2(2^m-1)a(m)\) is telescoped over \(p-1\) terms: every odd prime \(p\mid n\) of a composite \(n\) is thereby forced to divide \(a(n-1)\), contradicting the hypothesis, while the remaining powers of two are excluded by \(v_2(a(2^e-1))=e-1\). Once \(n\) is prime, an order \(d=\operatorname{ord}_n(2)<n-1\) makes the factor \(2^d-1\) force \(n\mid a(n-1)\), giving the same contradiction, so \(d=n-1\).
